**Your microphone on the PC, with any host.** Talk in Discord or in-game voice chat through your Android device while you stream, with Vibepollo, Sunshine or Apollo as they are. No different host needed.

### Microphone
- Starwire sends your voice to a small receiver on the PC, which plays it into VB-Cable, a free virtual microphone. Discord or the game picks it up as a normal mic, and your host doesn't change.
- Starwire turns on the device's echo cancelling and noise reduction where it has them. If teammates still hear the game, wear headphones.
- Local network only: the audio isn't encrypted, so Starwire only sends it to a PC on your local network or over a private VPN like Tailscale (which encrypts it).
- Running [logabell's Apollo build](https://github.com/logabell/apollo-microphone/releases)? Set **Send my microphone to** to **The PC's streaming app** and the microphone goes over the stream itself. Thanks to logabell for that code.

### Set up the microphone (once)
1. On the PC (Windows 10 or 11), download **Starwire-Microphone-for-Windows.zip** below and unzip it.
2. Double-click **setup-microphone.cmd**. If Windows warns about a downloaded file, choose **More info → Run anyway** (or **Run**), then allow it to make changes.
3. If VB-Cable isn't installed yet, the setup downloads it from VB-Audio, checks VB-Audio signed it and opens its installer: click **Install Driver**, then close it. Restart Windows only if the setup says VB-Cable isn't showing up.
4. The setup then builds the receiver, lets it through Windows Firewall for local-network and private VPN addresses only, starts it (no window, just an icon by the clock, also at every sign-in) and plays a test tone through VB-Cable to check it works.
5. In Discord or the game, choose **CABLE Output (VB-Audio Virtual Cable)** as the microphone.
6. In Starwire, turn on **Settings → Sound & vibration → Send my microphone**. From then on the mic starts with every stream.

Right-click the receiver's icon to check the virtual mic, play a test tone (for Discord's mic test) or quit. The [full guide](https://github.com/SicarioGaming/Starwire/tree/main/windows#readme) covers the details, troubleshooting and removal.

### What's in the Windows zip
- `setup-microphone.cmd`: the file to double-click. It runs the PowerShell setup below for that one run and asks for administrator rights.
- `setup-microphone.ps1`: the setup itself, about 300 lines. Safe to run again. Add `-Uninstall` (for example `setup-microphone.cmd -Uninstall`) to remove the receiver, its firewall rule and its startup entry, `-NoStartup` to stop it starting at sign-in, or `-Port` / `-StreamName` to change what it listens for.
- `StarwireMicReceiver.cs`: the receiver's source. The setup builds it on your PC with the C# compiler that comes with Windows, so there's no prebuilt .exe to trust.
- `starwire-mic.ico`: the receiver's icon.
- `README.md`: the full guide.

VB-Cable stays installed if you remove the receiver; take it off with its own setup (**Remove Driver**).

### Android devices
- Settings now show on narrow screens. On a small device held upright or a Galaxy Z Fold's cover screen they were blank.
- The game screen fits small screens: a smaller cover and title, and the Play and settings buttons stack.
- The top of the game screen scrolls away with your games. On a small screen held sideways it used to fill most of the screen. Once it's gone, a slim bar keeps the selected game and its Play button at the top; tap the bar to scroll back up.
- On a small screen held sideways, the stream menu puts Close, Quit and Disconnect on one row, so more tools fit.
- On a foldable's inner screen, the stream follows how you hold it instead of forcing landscape, which could leave it small with black borders.

### Game screen
- A Quit button sits beside Resume while a game is running, so you don't have to long-press the tile.
- Games without cover art each get their own take on the Starwire tile (colour, ring, moon, glow) instead of all looking the same.
- Softer corners, covers that arrive one after another and give a little when you press them, and a gently floating cover. The screen's animations pause while you stream.

### Settings and the stream menu
- Settings that change latency, smoothness, picture quality or battery have a short **Impact:** line under them, so you can see what turning one on or up gains or costs.
- The floating menu button is smaller, see-through until you touch it, and closes the menu as well as opening it.
- Menu items that switch something on or off (Stats, Mouse mode, Keyboard, Pan and zoom, Touch sensitivity, On-screen controller, Menu button) show a small switch, and tapping them keeps the menu open.
- The menu header shows the game's cover art. Desktop and games without cover art get a Starwire tile.
- The Lite stats line uses plain words: data rate, ping, decode time, dropped frames and FPS.

### Fixes
- Tapping a running Desktop tile to reconnect no longer crashes the app (the Resume button already worked), and neither does long-pressing Desktop or another icon tile. Create shortcut now works for them too.

### Install
- **Starwire-0.2.0.apk**: the Android app. Download it on your Android device and open it. It installs over 0.1.x and keeps your pairing and settings.
- **Starwire-Microphone-for-Windows.zip**: the PC side of the microphone (see above). Only needed if you want to use your mic.
